Claire — thanks, attaching a completed worksheet to start (AsterHealth_DR_Worksheet.xlsx). High level answers below; Karthik (solutions engineering) is looped in for low-level/runtime details and a runbook excerpt.

High-level:
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): RTO target for service continuity during region outage: 3–7 minutes for inbound traffic to be routed and steady-state request throughput to return.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity in Dedicated pools): RTO target: 1–3 minutes for automated failover within the same cloud provider region pair for pre-warmed pools; 5–10 minutes for cross-region cold starts if new capacity must be provisioned.
- RPO: for stateless inference traffic (typical token generation) RPO is near-zero — we do not persist model state across requests. For customer-managed session state (optional), RPO depends on your session store configuration; recommended pattern below.

Short asks for you: please confirm whether AsterHealth will use Redwood-hosted session tokens or an external session store (Redis in your VPC). If external store: we provide connection guidance for replication across regions.

Attachments: AsterHealth_DR_Worksheet.xlsx (first draft), SOC2 summary referenced. Will follow up with detailed failover sequencing (Karthik).

Thanks,

Claire — adding technical details from the runtime and orchestration side. Below are the concrete behaviors you can expect and the failover playbook excerpt (also attached).

1) Failure modes & RTO/RPO summary (concrete):
- Control-plane outage (hosted API control plane degraded):
  - Automated regional routing: inbound routing moves to healthy regions via global load-balancers and DNS failover. Observed median time to first successful request in acceptance tests: ~95 seconds (95th percentile < 180s) for common endpoints.
  - RTO (practical): 90s–3m for request routing + reconnection; additional ramp to steady throughput as caches warm.
- Node-level GPU failure within Dedicated pool:
  - Transparent request rerouting to other nodes in the same pool with minimal connection retries; median failover < 30s.
- Cross-region full-region outage (capacity rebuild required):
  - If Dedicated pool is pre-warmed and replicated, cross-region failover can be achieved in 60–300s. If capacity must be provisioned, worst-case warm-up (model spin + cache) is 5–10 minutes depending on model size/quantization.
- RPO:
  - Stateless inference: RPO = 0 for the service (no persisted generation state).
  - Stateful workflows (customer sessions): RPO = as configured on your session store. For near-zero RPO use cross-region synchronous replication or CRDT/append-only pattern.

2) Failover sequencing (short runbook excerpt):
- Detection: multi-signal health checks (control-plane metrics, region-level telemetry) -> automatic alerting.
- Automatic routing: DNS + global LB rebalancing to healthy endpoints.
- Model fallback: if the requested model variant is unavailable, policy-driven fallback to an operational variant (we include semantic equivalence notes in the model catalog).
- KV/prefix cache warming: automated prefix seeding for known hot prompts; cold cache after full failover has measurable latency effects for the first 10k tokens.
- Customer-facing impact: brief increase in per-token latency for first few hundred requests post-failover; we recommend client retry with exponential backoff and idempotent request patterns for long-running sessions.

3) Testing & evidence:
- We perform quarterly full-region failover tests for Dedicated customers under contract (we can provide the test report — attached dr_test_report_q1_2026.pdf).
- Hosted API undergoes simulated region degradation and canary failover drills every 6 months; we capture telemetry and SLO regressions in the console.

4) Encryption & KMS behavior:
- Data-in-transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS options for Private deployments.
- Data-at-rest: model artifacts and logs encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys (Private / Dedicated options). During failover, key access is preserved via cross-region key replicas where supported; otherwise, we provide documented procedures to rehydrate keys in the DR region (requires admin action for Dedicated/Private).

5) Operational recommendations for AsterHealth:
- For strict RPO requirements, host session state in your VPC Redis with cross-region replication and point Redwood at that store.
- For zero-maintenance, use Redwood Dedicated with pre-warmed, region-replicated pools.

Attached: failover_runbook_excerpt.txt (excerpt), dr_test_report_q1_2026.pdf

Happy to do a 45-minute tabletop next week with your infra and security teams.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Claire — answers below and attached artifacts: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf and the auditor-friendly runbook excerpt link.

1) KMS cross-region replicas:
- AWS KMS (Multi-Region Keys) — supported in us-east-1 <-> us-west-2 pairs and us-east-1 <-> eu-west-1 for customers on our Private offering with key replication enabled.
- GCP KMS (External Key Manager) — supported via customer-managed key replication patterns; requires customer configuration for cross-region replication.
- Azure Key Vault — we rely on geo-redundant key vault replication where the customer's subscription supports it; documentation included in the SOC pack.

2) Pre-warmed Dedicated pools:
- Exercise cadence: warm images are spot-validated weekly and fully exercised during quarterly DR drills.
- Warm images: immutable model artifacts and container images are stored as tagged snapshots; autoscaling uses those snapshots to spin additional capacity.

3) DR test playbook: attached (dr_test_report_q1_2026.pdf) includes steps, success criteria, and executive summary. We also maintain a redacted archive of past DR drills for auditors; link in the pack.

4) Data loss: there have been no production incidents in the past 24 months that resulted in customer data loss. We capture all incident postmortems in our incident tracker and redact customer-identifying details for audit bundles.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded the auditor artifacts to the shared drive (link above).
- We recommend a tabletop to walk through failover sequencing for your app topology; available slots next week (Feb 17–19). 

If you want a short one-page attestation for procurement, Marissa can prepare a template and we'll sign it.

Regards,
Olga
